title: Feature
description: A thing the product does, serving one or more Capabilities. The contract boundary: Stories and Acceptance Criteria hang off a Feature, not off each other. Source: supabase/migrations/003_feature.sql

product_id.description: FK -> product.id, denormalized (a feature reaches its product through capability). Exists so triggers can reject a feature linked to capabilities from two different products. IMMUTABLE after insert.

key.description: Slug, unique per (product_id, key). Stored as citext, so uniqueness is CASE-INSENSITIVE. The kebab-case pattern is project convention (e.g. 'session-cost-breakdown-by-token-type'), not a database CHECK.

deprecated_at.description: Nullable. Not automatically synchronized with lifecycle_state by the database.

removed_at.description: Nullable. Not automatically synchronized with lifecycle_state by the database.

value_prop.description: The case for building this feature. NOT the same thing as capability.value_prop, which is text and states a promise to a customer; this is jsonb and states why the work is worth doing. Shape is a database CHECK — every heading present, every heading an array. Content is prose and is not validated. Null means unplanned, which is legal.

cost_assessment.description: What building it costs, as prose grouped by kind. Shape enforced by CHECK; null legal.

scope_boundary.description: What this feature covers and explicitly does not. The out_of_scope side is the half that prevents two features from quietly claiming the same ground. Shape enforced by CHECK; null legal.

$comment: INVARIANT NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: every feature must belong to at least one capability, enforced by a DEFERRED constraint trigger that fires at COMMIT (insert on feature; delete on capability_has_feature; update of capability_has_feature.feature_id). A feature row is therefore only valid as part of a transaction that also writes its capability_has_feature link(s).
